1: [![build-openlane-sky130](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=master&event=push)](https://github.com/secworks/aes/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
2: 
3: aes
4: ===
5: 
6: Verilog implementation of the [symmetric block cipher AES (NIST FIPS 197)](http://csrc.nist.gov/publications/fips/fips197/fips-197.pdf).
7: 
8: 
9: ## Status ##
10: The core is completed, has been used in several FPGA and ASIC
11: designs. The core is well tested and mature.
12: 
13: 
14: ## Introduction ##
15: 
16: This implementation supports 128 and 256 bit keys. The
17: implementation is iterative and process one 128 block at a time. Blocks
18: are processed on a word level with 4 S-boxes in the data path. The
19: S-boxes for encryption are shared with the key expansion and the core
20: can thus not do key update in parallel with block processing.
21: 
22: The encipher and decipher block processing datapaths are separated and
23: basically self contained given access to a set of round keys and a
24: block. This makes it possible to hard wire the core to only encipher or
25: decipher operation. This allows the synthesis/build tools to optimize
26: away the other functionality which will reduce the size to about
27: 50%. This has been tested to verify that decryption is removed and the
28: core still works.
29: 
30: For cipher modes such as CTR, CCM, CMAC, GCM the decryption
31: functionality in the AES core will never be used and thus the decipher
32: block processing can be removed.
33: 
34: This is a fairly compact implementation. Further reduction could be
35: achived by just having a single S-box. Similarly the performane can be
36: increased by having 8 or even 16 S-boxes which would reduce the number
37: of cycles to two cycles for each round.
38: 
39: 
40: ### Contact information ##
41: 
42: Assured provides customer support including customization, integration
43: and system development related to the core. For more information,
44: please contact [Assured Security
45: Consultants](https://www.assured.se/contact).
46: 
47: 
48: ## Branches ##
49: 
50: There are several branches available that provides different versions of
51: the core. The branches are not planned to be merged into master. The
52: branches available that provides versions of the core are:
53: 
54: 
55: ### on-the-fly-keygen ###
56: 
57: This version of AES implements the key expansion using an on-the-fly
58: mechanism. This allows the initial key expansion to be removed. This
59: saves a number of cycles and also remove almost 1800 registers needed to
60: store the round keys. Note that this version of AES only supports
61: encryption. On-the-fly key generation does not work with
62: decryption. Decryption must be handled by the block cipher mode - for
63: example CTR.
64: 
65: 
66: ### dual-keys ###
67: 
68: This version of AES supports two separate banks of expanded keys to
69: allow fast key switching between two keys. This is useful for example in
70: an AEAD mode with CBC + CMAC implemented using a single AES core.
71: 
72: 
73: ### cmt-sbox ###
74: 
75: An experimental version of the core in which the S-box is implemented
76: using circuit minimized logic functions of a ROM table. The specific
77: table used is
78: [the 113 gate circuit](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/SLP_AES_113.txt) by the [CMT team at Yale](http://cs-www.cs.yale.edu/homes/peralta/CircuitStuff/CMT.html).
79: 
80: Some area and performance results using the cmt_sbox compared to
81: master:
82: 
83: #### Altera
84: - Tool: Quartus Prime 19.1.0
85: - Device: Cyclone V (5CGXFC7C7F23C8)
86: - master (S-box implemented with a table)
87:   - ALMs: 2599
88:   - Regs: 3184
89:   - Fmax: 93 MHz
90:   - aes_sbox: 160 ALUTs
91: 
92: - cmt_sbox
93:   - ALMs: 2759
94:   - Regs: 3147
95:   - Fmax: 69 MHz
96:   - aes_sbox: 363 ALUTs
97: 
98: 
99: #### Xilinx
100: - Tool: Vivado 2019.2
101: - Device: Kintex-7 (7k70tfbv676-1)
102: - master:
103:   - LUTs: 3020
104:   - FFs: 2992
105:   - Fmax: 125 MHz
106: 
107: - cmt_sbox:
108:   - LUTs: 2955
109:   - FFs: 2992
110:   - Fmax: 105 MHz
111: 
112: 
113: ## Core Usage
114: 
115: ### Usage sequence:
116: 1. Load the key to be used by writing to the key register words.
117: 2. Set the key length by writing to the config register.
118: 3. Initialize key expansion by writing a one to the init bit in the control register.
119: 4. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the key expansion has been completed.
120: 5. Write the cleartext block to the block registers.
121: 6. Start block processing by writing a one to the next bit in the control register.
122: 7. Wait for the ready bit in the status register to be cleared and then to be set again. This means that the data block has been processed.
123: 8. Read out the ciphertext block from the result registers.
124: 
125: 
126: ## FuseSoC
127: This core is supported by the
128: [FuseSoC](https://github.com/olofk/fusesoc) core package manager and
129: build system. Some quick  FuseSoC instructions:
130: 
131: install FuseSoC
132: ~~~
133: pip install fusesoc
134: ~~~
135: 
136: Create and enter a new workspace
137: ~~~
138: mkdir workspace && cd workspace
139: ~~~
140: 
141: Register aes as a library in the workspace
142: ~~~
143: fusesoc library add aes /path/to/aes
144: ~~~
145: 
146: ...if repo is available locally or...
147: ...to get the upstream repo
148: ~~~
149: fusesoc library add aes https://github.com/secworks/aes
150: ~~~
151: 
152: To run lint
153: ~~~
154: fusesoc run --target=lint secworks:crypto:aes
155: ~~~
156: 
157: Run tb_aes testbench
158: ~~~
159: fusesoc run --target=tb_aes secworks:crypto:aes
160: ~~~
161: 
162: Run with modelsim instead of default tool (icarus)
163: ~~~
164: fusesoc run --target=tb_aes --tool=modelsim secworks:crypto:aes
165: ~~~
166: 
167: List all targets
168: ~~~
169: fusesoc core show secworks:crypto:aes
170: ~~~
171: 
172: 
173: ## Implementation results - ASIC ##
174: 
175: The core has been implemented in standard cell ASIC processes.
176: 
177: ### TSMC 180 nm ###
178: Target frequency: 20 MHz
179: Complete flow from RTL to placed gates. Automatic clock gating and scan
180: insertion.
181: 
182: - 8 kCells
183: - Aera: 520 x 520 um
184: - Good timing margin with no big cells and buffers.
185: 
186: 
187: ## Implementation results - FPGA ##
188: 
189: The core has been implemented in Altera and Xilinx FPGA devices.
190: 
191: ### Altera Cyclone V GX ###
192: - 2624 ALMs
193: - 3123 Regs
194: - 96 MHz
195: - 46 cycles/block
196: 
197: 
198: ### Altera Cyclone IV GX ###
199: - 7426 LEs
200: - 2994 Regs
201: - 96 MHz fmax
202: - 46 cycles/block
203: 
204: This means that we can do more than 2 Mblocks/s or 256 Mbps
205: performance.
206: 
207: Removing the decipher module yields:
208: - 5497 LEs
209: - 2855 Regs
210: - 106 MHz fmax
211: - 46 cycles/block
212: 
213: 
214: ### Microchip IGLOO 2 ###
215: - Tool: Libero v 12.4
216: - Device: M2GL090TS-1FG484I
217: - LUTs: 6335
218: - SLEs: 1376
219: - BRAMs: 8
220: - Fmax: 98.5 MHz
221: 
222: 
223: ### Xilinx Spartan6LX-3 ###
224: - 2576 slices
225: - 3000 regs
226: - 100 MHz
227: - 46 cycles/block
228: 
229: 
230: ### Xilinx Artix 7 200T-3 ###
231: - 2298 slices
232: - 2989 regs
233: - 97 MHz
234: - 46 cycles/block

79:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
80:   // Device Under Test.
81:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
82:   aes_core dut(
83:                .clk(tb_clk),
84:                .reset_n(tb_reset_n),
85: 
86:                .encdec(tb_encdec),

250:   // point set the flag.

252:   task wait_ready;
253:     begin
254:       while (!tb_ready)

272:   // when the dut is actively processing a block and will in fact
273:   // at some point set the flag.

275:   task wait_valid;

291:                                   input           encdec,
292:                                   input [255 : 0] key,
293:                                   input           key_length,
294:                                   input [127 : 0] block,

302:      tb_keylen = key_length;
303:      tb_init = 1;
304:      #(2 * CLK_PERIOD);
305:      tb_init = 0;
306:      wait_ready();

308:      $display("Key expansion done");
309:      $display("");

314:      // Perform encipher och decipher operation on the block.
315:      tb_encdec = encdec;
316:      tb_block = block;
317:      tb_next = 1;
318:      #(2 * CLK_PERIOD);
319:      tb_next = 0;
320:      wait_ready();
321: 
322:      if (tb_result == expected)
323:        begin
324:          $display("*** TC %0d successful.", tc_number);
325:          $display("");
326:        end
327:      else
328:        begin
329:          $display("*** ERROR: TC %0d NOT successful.", tc_number);
330:          $display("Expected: 0x%032x", expected);
331:          $display("Got:      0x%032x", tb_result);

354:   initial
355:     begin : aes_core_test

41: module tb_aes_key_mem();
42: 
43:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
44:   // Internal constant and parameter definitions.
45:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
46:   parameter DEBUG = 1;
47:   parameter SHOW_SBOX = 0;
48: 
49:   parameter CLK_HALF_PERIOD = 1;
50:   parameter CLK_PERIOD = 2 * CLK_HALF_PERIOD;
51: 
52:   parameter AES_128_BIT_KEY = 0;
53:   parameter AES_256_BIT_KEY = 1;
54: 
55:   parameter AES_128_NUM_ROUNDS = 10;
56:   parameter AES_256_NUM_ROUNDS = 14;
57: 
58:   parameter AES_DECIPHER = 1'b0;
59:   parameter AES_ENCIPHER = 1'b1;
60: 
61: 
62:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
63:   // Register and Wire declarations.
64:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
65:   reg [31 : 0] cycle_ctr;
66:   reg [31 : 0] error_ctr;
67:   reg [31 : 0] tc_ctr;
68: 
69:   reg            tb_clk;
70:   reg            tb_reset_n;
71:   reg [255 : 0]  tb_key;
72:   reg            tb_keylen;
73:   reg            tb_init;
74:   reg [3 : 0]    tb_round;
75:   wire [127 : 0] tb_round_key;
76:   wire           tb_ready;
77: 
78:   wire [31 : 0]  tb_sboxw;
79:   wire [31 : 0]  tb_new_sboxw;
80: 
81: 
82:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
83:   // Device Under Test.
84:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
85:   aes_key_mem dut(
86:                   .clk(tb_clk),
87:                   .reset_n(tb_reset_n),
88: 
89:                   .key(tb_key),
90:                   .keylen(tb_keylen),
91:                   .init(tb_init),
92: 
93:                   .round(tb_round),
94:                   .round_key(tb_round_key),
95:                   .ready(tb_ready),
96: 
97:                   .sboxw(tb_sboxw),
98:                   .new_sboxw(tb_new_sboxw)
99:                  );
100: 
101:   // The DUT requirees Sboxes.
102:   aes_sbox sbox(.sboxw(tb_sboxw), .new_sboxw(tb_new_sboxw));
103: 
104: 
105:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
106:   // clk_gen
107:   //
108:   // Always running clock generator process.
109:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
110:   always
111:     begin : clk_gen
112:       #CLK_HALF_PERIOD;
113:       tb_clk = !tb_clk;
114:     end // clk_gen
115: 
116: 
117:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
118:   // sys_monitor()
119:   //
120:   // An always running process that creates a cycle counter and
121:   // conditionally displays information about the DUT.
122:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
123:   always
124:     begin : sys_monitor
125:       cycle_ctr = cycle_ctr + 1;
126:       #(CLK_PERIOD);
127:       if (DEBUG)
128:         begin
129:           dump_dut_state();
130:         end
131:     end

134:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
135:   // dump_dut_state()
136:   //
137:   // Dump the state of the dump when needed.
138:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
139:   task dump_dut_state;
140:     begin
141:       $display("State of DUT");
142:       $display("------------");
143:       $display("Inputs and outputs:");
144:       $display("key       = 0x%032x", dut.key);
145:       $display("keylen    = 0x%01x, init = 0x%01x, ready = 0x%01x",
146:                dut.keylen, dut.init, dut.ready);
147:       $display("round     = 0x%02x", dut.round);
148:       $display("round_key = 0x%016x", dut.round_key);
149:       $display("");
150: 
151:       $display("Internal states:");
152:       $display("key_mem_ctrl = 0x%01x, round_key_update = 0x%01x, round_ctr_reg = 0x%01x",
153:                dut.key_mem_ctrl_reg, dut.round_key_update, dut.round_ctr_reg);
154: 
155:       $display("prev_key0_reg = 0x%016x, prev_key0_new = 0x%016x, prev_key0_we = 0x%01x",
156:                dut.prev_key0_reg, dut.prev_key0_new, dut.prev_key0_we);
157:       $display("prev_key1_reg = 0x%016x, prev_key1_new = 0x%016x, prev_key1_we = 0x%01x",
158:                dut.prev_key1_reg, dut.prev_key1_new, dut.prev_key1_we);
159: 
160:       $display("rcon_reg = 0x%01x, rcon_new = 0x%01x,  rcon_set = 0x%01x,  rcon_next = 0x%01x, rcon_we = 0x%01x",
161:                dut.rcon_reg, dut.rcon_new, dut.rcon_set, dut.rcon_next, dut.rcon_we);
162: 
163:       $display("w0 = 0x%04x, w1 = 0x%04x, w2 = 0x%04x, w3 = 0x%04x",
164:                dut.round_key_gen.w0, dut.round_key_gen.w1,
165:                dut.round_key_gen.w2, dut.round_key_gen.w3);
166:       $display("w4 = 0x%04x, w5 = 0x%04x, w6 = 0x%04x, w7 = 0x%04x",
167:                dut.round_key_gen.w4, dut.round_key_gen.w5,
168:                dut.round_key_gen.w6, dut.round_key_gen.w7);
169:       $display("sboxw = 0x%04x, new_sboxw = 0x%04x, rconw = 0x%04x",
170:                dut.sboxw, dut.new_sboxw, dut.round_key_gen.rconw);
171:       $display("tw = 0x%04x, trw = 0x%04x", dut.round_key_gen.tw, dut.round_key_gen.trw);
172:       $display("key_mem_new = 0x%016x, key_mem_we = 0x%01x",
173:                dut.key_mem_new, dut.key_mem_we);
174:       $display("");
175: 
176:       if (SHOW_SBOX)
177:         begin
178:           $display("Sbox functionality:");
179:           $display("sboxw = 0x%08x", sbox.sboxw);
180:           $display("tmp_new_sbox0 = 0x%02x, tmp_new_sbox1 = 0x%02x, tmp_new_sbox2 = 0x%02x, tmp_new_sbox3",
181:                    sbox.tmp_new_sbox0, sbox.tmp_new_sbox1, sbox.tmp_new_sbox2, sbox.tmp_new_sbox3);
182:           $display("new_sboxw = 0x%08x", sbox.new_sboxw);
183:           $display("");
184:         end
185:     end
186:   endtask // dump_dut_state

189:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
190:   // reset_dut()
191:   //

193:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
194:   task reset_dut;
195:     begin

210:   task init_sim;

212:       cycle_ctr = 0;
213:       error_ctr = 0;
214:       tc_ctr    = 0;
215: 
216:       tb_clk     = 0;
217:       tb_reset_n = 1;
218:       tb_key     = {8{32'h00000000}};
219:       tb_keylen  = 0;
220:       tb_init    = 0;

222:     end

226:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
227:   // wait_ready()
228:   //
229:   // Wait for the ready flag in the dut to be set.
230:   //
231:   // Note: It is the callers responsibility to call the function
232:   // when the dut is actively processing and will in fact at some
233:   // point set the flag.
234:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
235:   task wait_ready;
236:     begin
237:       while (!tb_ready)
238:         begin
239:           #(CLK_PERIOD);
240:         end
241:     end
242:   endtask // wait_ready
243: 
244: 
245:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
246:   // check_key()
247:   //
248:   // Check a given key in the dut key memory against a given
249:   // expected key.
250:   //----------------------------------------------------------------
251:   task check_key(input [3 : 0] key_nr, input [127 : 0] expected);
252:     begin
253:       tb_round = key_nr;
254:       #(CLK_PERIOD);
255:       if (tb_round_key == expected)
256:         begin
257:           $display("** key 0x%01x matched expected round key.", key_nr);
258:           $display("** Got:      0x%016x **", tb_round_key);
259:         end
260:       else
261:         begin
262:           $display("** Error: key 0x%01x did not match expected round key. **", key_nr);
263:           $display("** Expected: 0x%016x **", expected);
264:           $display("** Got:      0x%016x **", tb_round_key);
265:           error_ctr = error_ctr + 1;
266:         end
267:       $display("");
268:     end
269:   endtask // check_key

98:     b0 = w >> 24

100:     b2 = w >> 8 & 0xff
101:     b3 = w & 0xff
102: 
103:     s0 = sbox[b0]
104:     s1 = sbox[b1]
105:     s2 = sbox[b2]

94: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
95: # substw()
96: #
97: # Returns a 32-bit word in which each of the bytes in the
98: # given 32-bit word has been used as lookup into the AES S-box.
99: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
100: def substw(w):
101:     b0 = w >> 24
102:     b1 = w >> 16 & 0xff
103:     b2 = w >> 8 & 0xff
104:     b3 = w & 0xff
105: 
106:     s0 = sbox[b0]
107:     s1 = sbox[b1]
108:     s2 = sbox[b2]
109:     s3 = sbox[b3]
110: 
111:     res = (s0 << 24) + (s1 << 16) + (s2 << 8) + s3
112: 
113:     if VERBOSE:
114:         print("Inside substw:")
115:         print("b0 = 0x%02x, b1 = 0x%02x, b2 = 0x%02x, b3 = 0x%02x" %
116:               (b0, b1, b2, b3))
117:         print("s0 = 0x%02x, s1 = 0x%02x, s2 = 0x%02x, s3 = 0x%02x" %
118:               (s0, s1, s2, s3))
119:         print("res = 0x%08x" % (res))
120: 
121:     return res
122: 
123: 
124: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
125: # rol8()
126: #
127: # Rotate the given 32 bit word 8 bits left.
128: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
129: def rol8(w):
130:     return ((w << 8) | (w >> 24)) & 0xffffffff
131:

133: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
134: # next_128bit_key()
135: #
136: # Generate the next four key words for aes-128 based on given
137: # rcon and previous key words.
138: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
139: def next_128bit_key(prev_key, rcon):
140:     (w0, w1, w2, w3) = prev_key
141: 
142:     rol = rol8(w3)
143:     subst = substw(rol)
144:     t = subst ^ (rcon << 24)
145: 
146:     k0 = w0 ^ t
147:     k1 = w1 ^ w0 ^ t
148:     k2 = w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t
149:     k3 = w3 ^ w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t
150: 
151:     if VERBOSE:
152:         print("Inside next 128bit key:")
153:         print("w0 = 0x%08x, w1 = 0x%08x, w2 = 0x%08x, w3 = 0x%08x" %
154:               (w0, w1, w2, w3))
155:         print("rol = 0x%08x, subst = 0x%08x, rcon = 0x%02x, t = 0x%08x" %
156:               (rol, subst, rcon, t))
157:         print("k0 = 0x%08x, k1 = 0x%08x, k2 = 0x%08x, k3 = 0x%08x" %
158:               (k0, k1, k2, k3))
159: 
160:     return (k0, k1, k2, k3)
161:

167: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
168: def key_gen128(key):
169:     round_keys = []
170: 
171:     round_keys.append(key)
172: 
173:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[0], get_rcon(1)))
174:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[1], get_rcon(2)))
175:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[2], get_rcon(3)))
176:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[3], get_rcon(4)))
177:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[4], get_rcon(5)))
178:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[5], get_rcon(6)))
179:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[6], get_rcon(7)))
180:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[7], get_rcon(8)))
181:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[8], get_rcon(9)))
182:     round_keys.append(next_128bit_key(round_keys[9], get_rcon(10)))
183: 
184:     return round_keys

187: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
188: # next_256bit_key_a()
189: #
190: # Generate the next four key words for aes-256 using algorithm A
191: # based on given rcon and the previous two keys.
192: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
193: def next_256it_key_a(key0, key1, rcon):
194:     (w0, w1, w2, w3) = key0
195:     (w4, w5, w6, w7) = key1
196: 
197:     sw = substw(rol8(w7))
198:     rw = (rcon << 24)
199:     t = sw ^ rw
200: 
201:     k0 = w0 ^ t
202:     k1 = w1 ^ w0 ^ t
203:     k2 = w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t
204:     k3 = w3 ^ w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t
205: 
206:     if (DUMP_VARS):
207:         print("next_256bit_key_a:")
208:         print("w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x" % (w0, w1, w2, w3))
209:         print("w4 = 0x%08x, w5 = 0x%08x, w6 = 0x%08x, w7 = 0x%08x" % (w4, w5, w6, w7))
210:         print("t = 0x%08x, sw = 0x%08x, rw = 0x%08x" % (t, sw, rw))
211:         print("k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x" % (k0, k1, k2, k3))
212:         print("")
213: 
214:     return (k0, k1, k2, k3)

217: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
218: # next_256bit_key_b()
219: #
220: # Generate the next four key words for aes-256 using algorithm B
221: # based on given previous eight keywords.
222: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
223: def next_256it_key_b(key0, key1):
224:     (w0, w1, w2, w3) = key0
225:     (w4, w5, w6, w7) = key1
226: 
227:     t = substw(w7)
228: 
229:     k0 = w0 ^ t
230:     k1 = w1 ^ w0 ^ t
231:     k2 = w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t
232:     k3 = w3 ^ w2 ^ w1 ^ w0 ^ t
233: 
234:     if (DUMP_VARS):
235:         print("next_256bit_key_b:")
236:         print("w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x, w0 = 0x%08x" % (w0, w1, w2, w3))
237:         print("w4 = 0x%08x, w5 = 0x%08x, w6 = 0x%08x, w7 = 0x%08x" % (w4, w5, w6, w7))
238:         print("t = 0x%08x" % (t))
239:         print("k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x, k0 = 0x%08x" % (k0, k1, k2, k3))
240:         print("")
241: 
242:     return (k0, k1, k2, k3)

245: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
246: # key_gen256()
247: #
248: # Generating the keys for 256 bit keys.
249: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
250: def key_gen256(key):
251:     round_keys = []
252:     (k0, k1, k2, k3, k4, k5, k6, k7) = key
253: 
254:     round_keys.append((k0, k1, k2, k3))
255:     round_keys.append((k4, k5, k6, k7))
256: 
257:     j = 1
258:     for i in range(0, (AES_256_ROUNDS - 2), 2):
259:         k = next_256it_key_a(round_keys[i], round_keys[i + 1], get_rcon(j))
260:         round_keys.append(k)
261:         k = next_256it_key_b(round_keys[i + 1], round_keys[i + 2])
262:         round_keys.append(k)
263:         j += 1
264: 
265:     # One final key needs to be generated.
266:     k = next_256it_key_a(round_keys[12], round_keys[13], get_rcon(7))
267:     round_keys.append(k)
268: 
269:     return round_keys

274: #
275: # The actual key generation.
276: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
277: def key_gen(key):
278:     if VERBOSE:
279:         print("Generating keys for AES-%d." % (len(key) * 32))
280: 
281:     if (len(key) * 32) == 128:
282:         return key_gen128(key)
283: 
284:     else:
285:         return key_gen256(key)

288: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
289: # get_rcon()
290: #
291: # Function implementation of rcon. Calculates rcon for a
292: # given round. This could be implemented as an iterator.
293: #-------------------------------------------------------------------
294: def get_rcon(round):
295:     rcon = 0x8d
296: 
297:     for i in range(0, round):
298:         rcon = ((rcon << 1) ^ (0x11b & - (rcon >> 7))) & 0xff
299: 
300:     return rcon
